## Requirement it fulfilled
# Substrate requirement: measurable-compact-argmin-selection

## Goal
Provide a reusable measurable nearest-point/argmin selector for a fixed nonempty compact subset of a finite-dimensional Euclidean space.

## Provides (API contract)
- `borelMeasurable_compact_argmin_selector`: for a nonempty compact action set `K` in finite-dimensional Euclidean space and a jointly Borel objective continuous in the action, expose a Borel measurable selector attaining the minimum whenever the standard measurable-extrema hypotheses hold.
- `borelMeasurable_nearestPoint_selector`: specialize the preceding result to squared Euclidean distance from a parameter point to `K`, returning a Borel measurable `π` with `π x ∈ K` and `dist x (π x) = inf_{y∈K} dist x y`.

## Statement / milestones
For a nonempty compact `K ⊆ EuclideanSpace ℝ ι` with finite `ι`, prove existence of a Borel measurable nearest-point selector on the ambient Euclidean space. If a faithful general compact-action measurable-argmin theorem can be built economically from available Mathlib measurable-multifunction machinery, expose it too; otherwise the nearest-point theorem is the required milestone. The selector must be total, attain the minimum exactly, and require no uniqueness or convexity.

## Standard reference
Brown and Purves (1973), *Measurable Selections of Extrema*, Annals of Statistics 1(5), Corollary 1, DOI 10.1214/aos/1176342510. The primary-source statement gives a Borel measurable exact minimizer on the set where the infimum is attained; compactness and continuity ensure attainment here.

## Intended reuse
The CausalSmith run `stat_proxy_effectlaw_eigencollision_frontier/v1` needs a Borel nearest-summary selector over a nonempty compact finite-dimensional summary closure. The result should be paper-agnostic and reusable for minimum-distance estimators, compact identified sets, and measurable projection rules.

## May assume / must derive
May assume finite-dimensional Euclidean ambient/action spaces, nonempty compactness of `K`, and standard Borel structures. Must derive exact minimum attainment, membership in `K`, totality, and Borel measurability of the selected rule. Do not assume a unique minimizer, convexity, or a measurable selector as an axiom.

## Non-goals (optional)
Universal measurable selection for arbitrary set-valued maps, infinite-dimensional actions, approximate selectors, and paper-specific summary-space definitions are out of scope.

## Known building blocks (optional)
Use existing compactness/continuity/minimum-attainment facts and any available measurable graph or finite-dimensional Borel infrastructure. Causalean's elementary interval/random-set selectors may provide patterns, but do not introduce a paper-module import.


## Your tools
- Read the staging files and inspect the Causalean tree (root = the directory containing `Causalean.lean`; sources under `Causalean/`).
- Project search — run from `CausalSmith/tools`: `npm run search -- "<concepts>"` (find existing decls to reuse/dedup against), `npm run search -- --scope module "<concepts>"` (find the correct topical HOME file/area — use this for placement), `npm run search -- --type "<pattern>"` / `--goal "<goal>"`.
- lean-lsp for signatures / declaration files.

## What to decide
1. PLACEMENT — merge-first. Find the substrate's natural topical home with `--scope module`. STRONGLY prefer MERGING each decl into an existing `Causalean/.../X.lean`; only CREATE a new topic file inside the narrowest faithful existing top-level subject area. Never invent a generic holding area. Target ≤600 lines; split before ~900 only for an independent topic/proof chain.
2. NAMESPACE — rewrite every `CausalSmith.Substrate.MeasurableCompactArgminSelection` reference to the chosen Causalean namespace (the namespace of the file it lands in).
3. REUSE / DEDUP — for each decl, search Causalean for one that already proves the SAME statement. If it exists, drop your reinvented version and use the existing one (add its import, point references at it). Reuse ONLY on genuine statement-equality — a rewire to a decl that merely looks similar will break the build. Dedup edits stay inside YOUR new content; never delete or alter an existing Causalean decl.

DOCUMENTATION (docstring-canonical) — every declaration that will render as a public library card gets a `/-- … -/` docstring whose FIRST paragraph is a self-contained natural-language translation for an econometrician with no Lean background (no Lean syntax, no field projections like `B.sigma` — say "the σ-algebra on B"; no "For every …" preamble restating the signature). This includes named local definitions or instances when the index extracts and displays them. `doc:gen` hard-fails if any published card would show “No natural-language translation yet.” Every new file opens with a `/-! … -/` module docstring stating what it provides. Theorem and lemma first paragraphs carry NL↔Lean CROSSLINKS: wrap the phrase translating each hypothesis or explicit binder in `[phrase](hyp:binderName)` (comma list `(hyp:h1,h2)` when one phrase covers several) and the conclusion phrase in `[phrase](goal)`, covering every binder and the conclusion; write the sentence to read naturally first, then bracket. `npm run lint:nl-links` is part of the integration gate and hard-fails on any incomplete or unannotated headline theorem.

   Use short names, e.g. `<repo-root>/CausalSmith/doc/study/measurable-compact-argmin-selection/coordinate_staging/round_1/foo.lean`, `<repo-root>/CausalSmith/doc/study/measurable-compact-argmin-selection/coordinate_staging/round_1/merge_x.lean`, `<repo-root>/CausalSmith/doc/study/measurable-compact-argmin-selection/coordinate_staging/round_1/area.json`. Put the EXACT bytes you want written/inserted into each staged file (namespaced, docstringed, ready to apply).
2. Emit ONLY a small JSON manifest that REFERENCES those staged files by `from` (relative to the staging dir). It contains no code — just short paths and one short anchor line per merge, so it always parses.

`{ "ops": [ … ], "notes": "<brief rationale>" }`. `target` paths are RELATIVE to the Causalean root. Op kinds:

- `{ "kind": "create_file", "target": "Causalean/…/Foo.lean", "from": "foo.lean", "newModule": "Causalean.….Foo" }` — write the staged `from` file as a NEW file at `target`. Set `newModule` (the Lean module name) ONLY for a new Lean module, so it is root-wired into `Causalean.lean`. Omit `newModule` for a new non-Lean record file.
- `{ "kind": "merge_lean", "target": "Causalean/…/X.lean", "anchor": "<a line already in X.lean>", "from": "merge_x.lean" }` — INSERT the staged `from` content after the first line containing `anchor` (empty anchor → append at end of file). INSERT-ONLY: the system preserves every existing byte and ROLLS BACK if a merge would change existing content. To add an import to an existing file, use a separate `merge_lean` anchored on an existing `import …` line (its `from` file holds just the import line). Multiple `merge_lean` ops may target the same file. If dependent inserts share one file/anchor, combine them into one staged file in dependency order, or anchor each later insert on text introduced by the prior one. Pick a SHORT, UNIQUE anchor line (a section header, a decl name) so it is unambiguous and easy to escape in JSON.
- `{ "kind": "write_file", "target": "doc/library_review/<Area>.json", "from": "area.json" }` — full-content write of a NON-Lean record file (headline sidecar, `doc/API.md`). Read the current file first, write the COMPLETE updated content to the staged `from` file (add entries/markers, never drop existing ones), and reference it here.

## Hard rules
- NEVER modify or delete an existing line in an existing Lean file. Integrating must be additive (new files + insert-only merges). If it genuinely requires editing an existing proven decl, do NOT — pick a different placement and explain in `notes`.
- Final Lean content may import and reference only Mathlib/Causalean modules. Rewrite every temporary staging reference; no `CausalSmith` import or qualified reference may remain in a staged create/merge body.
- Every `target` stays within the Causalean root; every `from` is a file you wrote under the staging dir.
- Do NOT run `lake build` / `library_index` / `embed` / `doc:gen` yourself — the system runs the full gate and rolls back on any failure. Emit only the manifest.
